messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christen,

Thanks for clarifying it for me. I am wondering if you could please mention some reference in this regard.

 ‘GPS does not have error autocorrelation for sampling interval of 1 minute or even down to 30 seconds.’

Thanks in advance,
Maraym

On Wednesday, May 30, 2018 at 3:11:09 AM UTC+2, Christen Fleming wrote:
> Hi Maryam,
>
> We do not yet model error autocorrelation. So far, for sampling down to 10-15 second intervals, I haven't personally seen any autocorrelation in modern GPS telemetry error, but I am about to look at some of new e-obs solar tags that collect 1 second data when the battery is full. I also know from the literature that older GPS data is supposed to have substantial error autocorrelation at under ~30 second intervals.
>
> For the future, when the kind of data that has autocorrelated error is being collected (maybe the new e-obs solar tags?), handling it will require calibration data to be collected. The HDOP values only account for the heteroskedasticity, not the autocorrelation. But, fortunately, the autocorrelation only emerges at very short timescales.
>
> Best,
> Chris
>
> On Tuesday, May 29, 2018 at 2:36:41 PM UTC-4, Maryam Teimouri wrote:
> >
> > Hi Chris,
> >
> >
> > I have a question regarding handling spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement errors in ctmm package.
> >
> > You take into account the autocorrelation of location data in the modeling, I am wondering if it includes autocorrelation of measurement errors as well.
> >
> > Are HDOP values enough for estimating the autocorrelation of measurement errors in the modeling?
> >
> >
> >
> > Thanks in advance,
> >
> > Maryam
> >

messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Maryam,

As with most things, you should check your own data. Recent development versions of ctmm on GitHub support the residuals() method on (calibrated) calibration data and you can feed that into the correlogram() method to check for autocorrelation.

But here is a reference on autocorrelation in L1-GPS data where they actually show a plot of the error ACF, which I don't think they standardized by DOP, but shows the autocorrelation dying off in around 50 seconds (Fig. 2).

Tao, Z., and P. Bonnifait. 2015. Modeling L1-GPS errors for an enhanced data fusion with
lane marking maps for road automated vehicles. In European Navigation Conference
(ENC 2015). Bordeaux, France.

I have not yet come across a calibration dataset collected at a higher rate than 5-10 seconds.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
Hi B.,

Is the output of ctmm's simulate function giving NA values? If so, I would rather fix that by you sending me a minimal working example (data + script).

Otherwise you could just store an intermediate vector for the rows that you intend to delete:

NAS <- apply(df,1,function(row) any(is.na <http://is.na>(row)) )

and then remove them from both data frames like

df <- df[!NAS,]

Best,
Chris
